questions.question: What is the difference between reversible and irreversible reactions?

options.A: In reversible reactions, the reaction goes to completion.
options.B: In irreversible reactions, there is a mixture of products and reactants.
options.C: In reversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.
options.D: In irreversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.

questions.explanation: Reversible reactions are those that can proceed in both forward and backward directions, eventually reaching a state of dynamic equilibrium where the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal, and there is a mixture of reactants and products present. Irreversible reactions proceed to completion, meaning nearly all reactants are converted to products, and equilibrium is not established.

questions.question: The general formula for saturated monocarboxylic acids is

options.A: RCOOH
options.B: RCOR
options.C: RCHO
options.D: ROR

questions.explanation: Saturated monocarboxylic acids have the general formula R-COOH, where R is a saturated alkyl group (or hydrogen in the case of formic acid). The carboxyl group (-COOH) is the functional group characteristic of carboxylic acids. RCOR is the general formula for ketones, RCHO for aldehydes, and ROR for ethers.

questions.question: What is enthalpy change? It is

options.A: the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure and volume.
options.B: the amount of heat absorbed in a reaction.
options.C: the amount of heat given out in a reaction.
options.D: the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure.

questions.explanation: Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the amount of heat energy absorbed or released by a chemical reaction at constant pressure. Many biological and chemical reactions occur at constant atmospheric pressure, making enthalpy a useful measure of heat change. Option A is incorrect because it mentions constant volume (which would be internal energy), while options B and C only describe one direction of heat flow.

questions.question: What is oxidation? Oxidation is

options.A: the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent.
options.B: the reduction of the oxidation state of the oxidizing agent.
options.C: the addition of hydrogen to a substance and the removal of oxygen from a substance.
options.D: the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.

questions.explanation: Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons by a species, which results in an increase in its oxidation number (state). This is the modern definition based on electron transfer. Option A describes reduction (gain of electrons). Option B is incorrect because the oxidizing agent is reduced (gains electrons) and its oxidation number decreases. Option C describes a classical definition of oxidation (addition of oxygen, removal of hydrogen).

questions.question: What is meant by preferential discharge, if a number of ions are present in a solution? It means that the one which requires

options.A: highest energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
options.B: highest energy will be liberated last at a given electrode.
options.C: least energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
options.D: least energy will be liberated last at a given electrode.

questions.explanation: Preferential discharge during electrolysis occurs when multiple ions are present. The ion that requires the least energy (i.e., the lowest electrode potential or overpotential) will be discharged at the electrode first. This is governed by the electrochemical series. Ions with higher discharge potentials (requiring more energy) will be liberated later or not at all until the more readily discharged ions are depleted.

questions.question: Faraday's Second Law states:

options.A: the amount of a substance consumed or produced at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the solution.
options.B: the amount of a substance consumed or produced at an electrode is inversely proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the solution.
options.C: passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their molecular masses.
options.D: passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their equivalent masses.

questions.explanation: Faraday's Second Law of Electrolysis states that when the same quantity of electricity is passed through solutions of different electrolytes, the masses of the substances produced or consumed are directly proportional to their chemical equivalent masses (equivalent weights). Option A describes Faraday's First Law. Options B and C are incorrectly stated.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Zn-Cu voltaic cell?

options.A: The electrons flow from right to left through the external circuit.
options.B: As the cell operates, electrons are continuously generated at the cathode and consumed at the anode.
options.C: The anode half-cell consists of Cu electrode dipped into a Cu²⁺ solution.
options.D: After the cell runs for several hours, the Zn electrode weights less.

questions.explanation: In a Zn-Cu voltaic (galvanic) cell, zinc (Zn) is the anode and undergoes oxidation: Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. This causes the zinc electrode to lose mass as it dissolves into the solution. The copper electrode is the cathode where reduction occurs: Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s), causing it to gain mass. Option A is incorrect as electrons flow from anode (Zn) to cathode (Cu). Option B is incorrect because electrons are not generated or consumed; they flow through the external circuit. Option C is incorrect because the Cu electrode is the cathode, not the anode.

questions.question: What is the significance of electron probability distribution? It tells us about

options.A: finding the electron very close to the nucleus at all times.
options.B: the probability of finding an electron is very far away from the nucleus.
options.C: the uncertainty to assign fixed path for electrons.
options.D: finding the electron in its orbit at a particular time.

questions.explanation: Electron probability distribution (from quantum mechanics) describes the probability of finding an electron in a particular region of space around the nucleus. This concept arises from the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle, which states that we cannot simultaneously know both the exact position and momentum of an electron. Therefore, we cannot assign a fixed path or orbit to electrons (as in the Bohr model). Instead, we describe regions of high probability (orbitals).

questions.question: Which group in the periodic table contains elements with the valence electron configuration of ns²np¹?

options.A: III
options.B: IV
options.C: I
options.D: II

questions.explanation: The valence electron configuration ns²np¹ indicates that there are three valence electrons (2 in the s orbital and 1 in the p orbital). Elements with three valence electrons are found in Group III (13 in the modern IUPAC numbering). Group I has ns¹, Group II has ns², and Group IV has ns²np².

questions.question: At 75°C, the vapor pressure of pure water is 39 kPa. Which one of the vapor pressure of a solution obtained by dissolving 34.2 g sucrose in 180 mL of water? (Assume that the density of water is 1.000 g/mL)

options.A: 41.1 kPa
options.B: 44.5 kPa
options.C: 31.2 kPa
options.D: 38.6 kPa

questions.explanation: This problem uses Raoult's Law: P_solution = X_solvent × P°_solvent. First, calculate moles of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁): molar mass = 342 g/mol, moles = 34.2/342 = 0.100 mol. Water mass = 180 mL × 1.00 g/mL = 180 g, moles water = 180/18 = 10.0 mol. Mole fraction of water = 10.0/(10.0+0.100) = 10.0/10.1 = 0.9901. P_solution = 0.9901 × 39 kPa = 38.6 kPa. The vapor pressure lowers because a non-volatile solute is added.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the colligative properties of electrolytes and non-electrolytes?

options.A: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is very low compared to electrolytes.
options.B: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is the same as those of electrolytes.
options.C: The effect of electrolytes on colligative properties is very high compared to non-electrolytes.
options.D: The colligative properties of non-electrolytes are not considerably changed.

questions.explanation: The statement that is NOT true is option B. Electrolytes have a much greater effect on colligative properties than non-electrolytes because they dissociate into multiple ions in solution, increasing the number of particles. Non-electrolytes do not dissociate, so they have a lower effect. Options A, C, and D correctly describe this relationship.

questions.question:
For the reaction shown below, which of the following is a conjugate acid-base pair?
HC₂O₄⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⟶ H₃O⁺ + C₂O₄²⁻

options.A: H₃O⁺ and HC₂O₄²⁻
options.B: HC₂O₄⁻ and C₂O₄²⁻
options.C: HC₂O₄⁻ and H₂O
options.D: H₂O and C₂O₄²⁻

questions.explanation: A conjugate acid-base pair consists of two species that differ by one proton (H⁺). HC₂O₄⁻ loses a proton to become C₂O₄²⁻, so they are a conjugate acid-base pair. H₂O gains a proton to become H₃O⁺, so H₂O and H₃O⁺ are another conjugate acid-base pair. Option B correctly identifies HC₂O₄⁻ and C₂O₄²⁻ as a conjugate pair.

questions.question: What is the purpose of synthetic cryolite in the extraction of aluminum by the Hall's process?

options.A: Cryolite increases the melting point of alumina.
options.B: Cryolite is used as a catalyst in the extraction of aluminum.
options.C: Cryolite increases the purity of the extracted aluminum.
options.D: Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.

questions.explanation: In the Hall-Héroult process for extracting aluminum, synthetic cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to alumina (Al₂O₃) to lower its melting point from about 2050°C to around 950°C, making the electrolysis process more economically feasible. Cryolite also increases the conductivity of the molten mixture. It does not act as a catalyst, nor does it directly increase purity.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical property of aluminum?

options.A: Aluminum is a good conductor of heat and electricity.
options.B: Aluminum has a lower density than any other commercial metal.
options.C: Aluminum liberates hydrogen gas from dilute acids like HCl and H₂SO₄.
options.D: Aluminum is a grey metal in color.

questions.explanation: A chemical property describes how a substance reacts with other substances. Aluminum's ability to liberate hydrogen gas when reacting with dilute acids is a chemical property. Options A, B, and D are physical properties (conductivity, density, color). The reaction with acids involves a chemical change: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂.

questions.question: How is tanning carried out? In tanning the hides or skins are

options.A: treated with chromium salts.
options.B: treated with dilute hydrochloric acid to remove the lime.
options.C: soaked in water for several days.
options.D: soaked in lime and water for several days.

questions.explanation: Tanning is the process of treating animal hides to produce leather. The most common modern method is chrome tanning, where hides are treated with chromium salts (specifically chromium(III) sulfate). This stabilizes the collagen proteins and prevents decomposition. Soaking in lime and water (option D) is a preparatory step called liming, not the tanning process itself.

questions.question: How can a project of establishing an industry that consumes coal affect the environment?

options.A: Production of high level of lead in the atmosphere
options.B: By changing the pH of water
options.C: Increment in concentration of nitric oxide
options.D: Rise in global temperature

questions.explanation: Coal combustion releases large amounts of carbon dioxide (CO₂), a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming and climate change. This leads to a rise in global temperature. While coal combustion can also release other pollutants (SO₂ causing acid rain, which changes water pH, and NOₓ), the most significant and global environmental impact is the rise in global temperature from CO₂ emissions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity SI unit?

options.A: Pressure
options.B: Length
options.C: Speed
options.D: Force

questions.explanation: Length is one of the seven fundamental (base) quantities in the SI system. The fundamental quantities are: length (meter), mass (kilogram), time (second), electric current (ampere), thermodynamic temperature (kelvin), amount of substance (mole), and luminous intensity (candela). Pressure, speed, and force are derived quantities.

questions.question: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory was modified by the modern atomic theory?

options.A: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions.
options.B: Compounds are formed when atoms of more than one element combine.
options.C: Atoms are the smallest particles of all elements.
options.D: Atoms are indivisible and indestructible.

questions.explanation: Dalton's postulate that atoms are indivisible and indestructible was modified with the discovery of subatomic particles (electrons, protons, neutrons). We now know atoms can be divided. Options A and B remain essentially valid in modern atomic theory. Option C was modified because atoms are not the smallest particles; they contain smaller subatomic particles.

questions.question: Which of the following includes all of the known atomic models?

options.A: Bohr Model, the Quantum Mechanical Model, Rutherford Model, Thomson Model, Dalton's Atomic Model
options.B: Bohr Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model, Dalton's Atomic Model, de Broglie Model
options.C: Bohr Model, Quantum Mechanical Model, Dalton's Atomic Model, Valence Bond Model
options.D: Bohr Model, the Quantum Mechanical Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model

questions.explanation: Option A correctly lists all the major historical atomic models in chronological order: Dalton's Atomic Model (solid sphere), Thomson Model (plum pudding), Rutherford Model (nuclear), Bohr Model (planetary), and the Quantum Mechanical Model (electron cloud). The de Broglie model and Valence Bond model are not considered comprehensive atomic structure models.

questions.question: The electron configuration of Cu (Z=29) is:

options.A: [Kr]4s²3d⁹
options.B: [Ar]4s¹3d¹⁰
options.C: [Ar]4s²3p⁸
options.D: [Ar]4s²4d⁹

questions.explanation: Copper (Cu, Z=29) has an anomalous electron configuration: [Ar]4s¹3d¹⁰ instead of the expected [Ar]4s²3d⁹. This is due to the extra stability of a completely filled d subshell (3d¹⁰). A half-filled or completely filled d subshell provides additional stability, so one electron from the 4s orbital moves to the 3d orbital. This is the correct configuration for copper.

questions.question: What does Mendeleev's Periodic Law state? Properties of elements are periodic functions of their

options.A: electron configurations.
options.B: atomic radius.
options.C: atomic numbers.
options.D: atomic masses.

questions.explanation: Mendeleev's Periodic Law stated that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses. Later, Henry Moseley revised this to state that properties are periodic functions of atomic numbers. Since this question specifically asks about Mendeleev's law (not the modern version), the correct answer is atomic masses.

questions.question:
What is the mole ratio of oxygen gas to carbon dioxide gas in the following reaction?
C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(l)

options.A: 2 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide
options.B: 7 mole oxygen gas to 5 mole carbon dioxide
options.C: 10 mole oxygen gas to 6 mole carbon dioxide
options.D: 5 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: From the balanced equation: 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g). The mole ratio of oxygen to carbon dioxide is 5:3. Option D correctly states this as 5 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide. Option C (10:6) is equivalent but simplified to 5:3; however, the question asks for the mole ratio, which should be expressed as the simplest whole number ratio.

questions.question:
Consider the following chemical equation for the combustion of ethane (C₂H₆) in the presence of oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water.
2C₂H₆(g) + 7O₂(g) → 4CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l)
In this reaction:

options.A: water is formed at a rate equal to 2/3 the rate of formation of CO₂
options.B: CO₂ is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed.
options.C: the rate of consumption of ethane is 7 times faster than the rate of consumption of oxygen.
options.D: the rate of formation of CO₂ equals the rate of formation of water.

questions.explanation: From the balanced equation: CO₂ is formed 4 moles for every 2 moles of ethane consumed, so CO₂ is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed (4:2 = 2:1). Option A is incorrect: water is formed 6 moles and CO₂ 4 moles, ratio 6:4 = 3:2, so water is formed at 1.5 times (not 2/3) the rate. Option C: ethane consumed at 2/7 the rate of oxygen. Option D: CO₂ and water are formed at different rates (4:6).

questions.question: Which of the following factors DOES NOT affect the rate of a reaction?

options.A: Temperature
options.B: Enthalpy
options.C: Concentration
options.D: Surface area

questions.explanation: Enthalpy (ΔH) is a thermodynamic property that measures the heat absorbed or released in a reaction. It does not affect the rate of reaction; it affects the equilibrium position and spontaneity. Temperature, concentration, and surface area all affect the rate of reaction. Enthalpy is a state function and does not appear in rate equations.

questions.question: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

options.A: By lowering the activation energy
options.B: By changing the equilibrium constant
options.C: By forming an intermediate complex
options.D: By increasing the activation energy

questions.explanation: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by lowering the activation energy (Eₐ), providing an alternative pathway with a lower energy barrier. Catalysts do not change the equilibrium constant (they affect forward and reverse rates equally). While catalysts may form intermediate complexes, this is a mechanism, not the reason for increased rate. They do not increase activation energy.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle's Law?

options.A: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
options.B: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
options.C: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is directly proportional to the applied pressure.
options.D: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the applied pressure.

questions.explanation: Boyle's Law states that at constant temperature, the volume of a fixed amount of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure: V ∝ 1/P, or PV = k (constant). As pressure increases, volume decreases proportionally. This is the fundamental relationship describing the pressure-volume behavior of ideal gases at constant temperature.

questions.question: What are intermolecular forces? They are forces due to the attraction between

options.A: nuclei and electron pair.
options.B: cations and delocalized electrons.
options.C: molecules.
options.D: cations and anions.

questions.explanation: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules (inter = between). These include London dispersion forces, dipole-dipole forces, and hydrogen bonding. Option A describes intramolecular forces within molecules (covalent bonds). Option B describes metallic bonding. Option D describes ionic bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to chemical bonding theories?

options.A: Molecular orbital theory and kinetic-molecular theory.
options.B: Valence bond theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory.
options.C: Kinetic-molecular theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory.
options.D: Valence bond theory and molecular orbital theory.

questions.explanation: Valence Bond (VB) theory and Molecular Orbital (MO) theory are the two main theories used to describe chemical bonding. VSEPR theory (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion) predicts molecular geometry but is not a bonding theory per se. The kinetic-molecular theory describes the behavior of gases, not chemical bonding.

questions.question: In which of the following molecules is the central atom sp² hybridized?

options.A: SO₂
options.B: CO
options.C: CO₂
options.D: N₂O

questions.explanation: In SO₂, the sulfur atom has three electron domains (two bonding pairs and one lone pair), making it sp² hybridized with a bent geometry. CO₂ has two electron domains (linear, sp hybridization). CO has two electron domains (linear, sp hybridization). N₂O (nitrous oxide) has two electron domains on the central N (sp hybridization).

questions.question: For a reaction: 1/2 A → 2B the rate of disappearance of A is related to the appearance of B by the expression:

options.A: Δ[A]/Δt = 1/2 Δ[B]/Δt
options.B: Δ[A]/Δt = 1/4 Δ[B]/Δt
options.C: Δ[A]/Δt = Δ[B]/Δt
options.D: Δ[A]/Δt = 4Δ[B]/Δt

questions.explanation: For the reaction 1/2 A → 2B, the stoichiometric ratio is: -Δ[A]/Δt = (1/2)/2 Δ[B]/Δt = 1/4 Δ[B]/Δt. This means A disappears at 1/4 the rate at which B appears. For every 1 mole of A consumed, 4 moles of B are produced (since 0.5 A → 2B, multiply by 2: A → 4B). Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.question: The half-life of a reaction is the time taken for the

options.A: rate constant to decrease by 50% of its initial value.
options.B: complete conversion of a reactant into a product.
options.C: reactant concentration to decrease by 50% of its initial value.
options.D: rate constant to increase by 50% of its initial value.

questions.explanation: The half-life (t₁/₂) of a reaction is the time required for the concentration of a reactant to decrease to half of its initial value. For first-order reactions, the half-life is constant and independent of initial concentration. The rate constant (k) is a constant for a given reaction at a given temperature and does not change over time.

questions.question:
For the conversion of 3.5 yards into meter using the factor label method, which of the following is the correct step?
1 yard = 3.5 feet; 1 foot = 12 inch; 1 inch = 2.54 cm; 1 m = 100 cm

options.A: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/1 foot)(1 in/2.54 m)(1m/100 cm)
options.B: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(1 foot/112 in)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1m/100 cm)
options.C: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/1 foot)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1m/100 cm)
options.D: (3.5 yards/1)(1 yard/3.5 feet)(12 in/1 foot)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1m/100 cm)

questions.explanation: The correct factor-label conversion should use conversion factors so that units cancel appropriately: yards → feet → inches → cm → meters. Starting with 3.5 yards, multiply by (3.5 feet/1 yard) to convert to feet, then (12 in/1 foot) to convert to inches, then (2.54 cm/1 in) to convert to cm, and finally (1 m/100 cm) to convert to meters. Option C has the correct sequence.

questions.question: In the scientific method, a predictive statement that can be tested experimentally is:

options.A: proof.
options.B: hypothesis.
options.C: truth.
options.D: evidence.

questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a predictive statement or proposed explanation that can be tested experimentally. It is an educated guess based on observations. A proof is established by experiments. Truth is a philosophical concept. Evidence is data collected during experiments. The hypothesis is central to the scientific method as it generates testable predictions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about cathode rays? Cathode rays

options.A: contain particles, which are positively charged.
options.B: are common constituents of all matter and their m/e is constant for all gases.
options.C: contain particles, which are negatively charged.
options.D: travel in straight lines from cathode to the anode.

questions.explanation: The statement that is NOT true is option A: cathode rays contain particles that are negatively charged (electrons), not positively charged. Cathode rays are streams of electrons that travel from the cathode to the anode, are common to all matter, and have a constant charge-to-mass ratio regardless of the gas used in the tube.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the energy of a photon?

options.A: It is directly related to the intensity of the light.
options.B: It is directly proportional to the wavelength of the light.
options.C: It is directly proportional to the observed frequency of the light.
options.D: It is inversely proportional to the observed frequency of the light.

questions.explanation: The energy of a photon is directly proportional to its frequency: E = hν (where h is Planck's constant and ν is frequency). Therefore, higher frequency means higher energy. Photon energy is inversely proportional to wavelength (E = hc/λ). Energy is not related to light intensity (which is a measure of the number of photons).

questions.question: Which of the following explains the emission spectra of atoms consisting of a series of fine lines?

options.A: The energy of the atoms is continuous with discreet frequencies.
options.B: An electron that revolves around the nucleus emits radiation.
options.C: An electron can have specific energy values in an atom.
options.D: An electron undergoes a transition by energy changes corresponding to photon of specific wavelength.

questions.explanation: Emission spectra consist of discrete lines because electrons can only occupy specific energy levels in atoms. When an electron transitions from a higher energy level to a lower one, it emits a photon with energy equal to the difference between the two levels. This results in specific wavelengths (colors) of light, appearing as distinct lines in the spectrum.

questions.question: Which of the following is a polytropic acid?

options.A: HF
options.B: HNO₃

questions.explanation: A polytropic acid (polyprotic acid) is an acid that can donate more than one proton per molecule. HNO₃ (nitric acid) is monoprotic (can donate only one proton). H₂SO₄ (sulfuric acid) is diprotic (can donate two protons), and H₃PO₄ (phosphoric acid) is triprotic (can donate three protons). Since this question only provides HF and HNO₃ as options, and both are monoprotic acids, I need to check the context. Nitric acid (HNO₃) is a strong acid, but it's monoprotic. The term "polytropic" here likely refers to "polyprotic," and among the options provided in the original exam, H₃PO₄ would be the answer. However, since only HF and HNO₃ are shown in the options, the question might be incomplete in the PDF extract.

questions.question: Which of the following does represent a general property of a base?

options.A: Soluble bases release hydronium ion in aqueous solution.
options.B: Aqueous solution of bases turns methyl orange into red.
options.C: Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity.
options.D: Aqueous solution of bases turns blue litmus paper to red.

questions.explanation: Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity because they dissociate completely into ions in aqueous solution. Option A is incorrect because bases release hydroxide ions (OH⁻), not hydronium ions (H₃O⁺). Option B is incorrect: bases turn methyl orange from red to yellow (they turn red litmus blue). Option D is incorrect: bases turn red litmus blue, not blue to red.

questions.question: What are salts? Salts are

options.A: ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid.
options.B: ionic compounds formed by partial replacement of ionizable hydroxide by metal cations.
options.C: ionic compounds formed by complete replacement of ionizable hydrogen by anions of the acid.
options.D: ionic compounds that result from the reaction between metal hydroxide and water.

questions.explanation: Salts are ionic compounds composed of cations (derived from a base) and anions (derived from an acid). They are formed by the neutralization reaction between an acid and a base. Option B describes basic salts. Option C describes normal (neutral) salts but the terminology is incorrect (hydrogen replaced by cations, not anions). Option D describes a simple neutralization reaction.

questions.question: The process in which a compound absorbs electrical energy and decomposes into its element is

options.A: hydrolysis.
options.B: electroplating.
options.C: electrolysis.
options.D: solvolysis.

questions.explanation: Electrolysis is the process where electrical energy causes a chemical decomposition of a compound into its elements (e.g., water decomposes into hydrogen and oxygen). Hydrolysis uses water for decomposition. Electroplating uses electrolysis to deposit a metal coating. Solvolysis uses a solvent (usually water) for decomposition.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about galvanic cells used in commercial lead storage batteries? In lead storage batteries,

options.A: half of the galvanic cells are connected in series.
options.B: the galvanic cells are made up of PbO₂ of anodes.
options.C: galvanic cells are connected in series.
options.D: galvanic cells are connected in parallel.

questions.explanation: In lead storage batteries, multiple galvanic cells (typically 6 cells) are connected in series to produce a higher total voltage. Each cell produces about 2V, and six cells in series give 12V. The cells are not connected in parallel (which would increase current but not voltage). The anode is lead (Pb), not PbO₂ (which is the cathode material).

questions.question:
The self-ionization of water can be expressed by the equation: H₂O(l) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
Which of the following is the correct expression of the ionic product of water?

options.A: K_w = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻]
options.B: K_w = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻][H₂O]
options.C: K_w = K_w(H₂O)²
options.D: K_w = K_w(H₂O)

questions.explanation: The ionic product of water (K_w) is expressed as K_w = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻]. At 25°C, K_w = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴. The concentration of water (H₂O) is essentially constant (55.5 M) and is incorporated into the K_w constant. Therefore, the correct expression does not include the concentration of water as a variable.

questions.question: What is the effect of a common ion in an electrolytic solution?

options.A: It decreases the solubility of a solute.
options.B: It has no effect on the pH of a solution.
options.C: It suppresses the imitation of a weak acid and raises the pH.
options.D: It suppresses the imitation of a weak base and lowers the pH.

questions.explanation: The common ion effect describes the decrease in solubility of an ionic compound when a salt containing a common ion is added to the solution. This is explained by Le Chatelier's principle. The common ion effect also affects the pH of weak acid/base solutions, suppressing ionization and shifting the equilibrium toward the molecular form.

questions.question: Sodium carbonate is a basic salt because it is a salt of

options.A: a weak acid and a weak base and the cation of the weak base can be hydrolyzed.
options.B: a strong acid and a weak base and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed.
options.C: a strong base and a weak acid and the anion of the weak acid can be hydrolyzed.
options.D: a strong base and a strong acid and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed.

questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is a basic salt formed from a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (H₂CO₃). The carbonate ion (CO₃²⁻), the anion of the weak acid, undergoes hydrolysis: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻. This produces hydroxide ions, making the solution basic. The cation (Na⁺) from a strong base does not undergo hydrolysis.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for an acid-base titration?

options.A: An acid-base titration is a method of quantitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base.
options.B: An acid-base titration is a method of qualitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base.
options.C: Indicators catalyze an acid-base titration to show the inflection point of the titration curve.
options.D: Acid-base titrations cannot be carried out in the absence of indicators.

questions.explanation: Acid-base titration is a quantitative analytical method used to determine the concentration of an acid or base. It is quantitative (not qualitative) because it provides numerical concentration values. Indicators do not catalyze the reaction; they indicate the endpoint (equivalence point) by changing color. Titrations can be conducted without indicators using pH meters.

questions.question: What is the change in internal energy (ΔE) for a reaction, in which the system absorbs 650 J of heat and 125 J of work is done on the system?
questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics states: ΔE = q + w, where q is heat absorbed (+) and w is work done on the system (+). Here, q = +650 J and w = +125 J. ΔE = 650 + 125 = 775 J. The internal energy increases by 775 J. Options A and B are negative, indicating energy loss, which is incorrect.

questions.question: Which statement describes the formation of a covalent bond? In covalent bond electrons are

options.A: shared between non-metallic atoms.
options.B: transferred from non-metallic atoms to metallic atoms.
options.C: shared between metallic atoms.
options.D: transferred from metallic atoms to non-metallic atoms.

questions.explanation: A covalent bond is formed when electrons are shared between non-metallic atoms. This sharing allows each atom to achieve a stable electron configuration. Option B and D describe ionic bonding (transfer of electrons from metal to non-metal). Option C describes metallic bonding.

questions.question: How do the elements of Group IIA form ions?

options.A: By losing 2 electrons
options.B: By gaining 2 electrons
options.C: By gaining one electron
options.D: By losing one electron

questions.explanation: Group IIA elements (alkaline earth metals) have two valence electrons (ns²). They form ions by losing these two electrons to achieve a noble gas configuration, resulting in 2+ ions (cations). For example, Mg → Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻. They do not gain electrons because they are metals and have low electronegativity.

questions.question: How is hydrogen bonding formed? It is formed when a hydrogen atom is bonded to

options.A: highly electronegative elements, chlorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
options.B: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
options.C: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and oxygen.
options.D: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and phosphorus.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding occurs when a hydrogen atom is covalently bonded to one of the three most electronegative elements: fluorine (F), oxygen (O), or nitrogen (N). The hydrogen atom carries a partial positive charge and can form electrostatic attractions with lone pairs on electronegative atoms. Chlorine and phosphorus are not electronegative enough for significant hydrogen bonding.

questions.question: Which one of the following of energy change occurs from the combustion of carbon in oxygen?

options.A: heat energy
options.B: solar energy
options.C: light energy
options.D: electrical energy

questions.explanation: The combustion of carbon in oxygen is an exothermic reaction that releases heat energy (and some light as a flame). The reaction is: C + O₂ → CO₂, ΔH = -393.5 kJ/mol. This is a chemical energy → heat energy conversion. While light is also produced, heat is the primary form of energy released.

questions.question: What is the molar volume of a gas?

options.A: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 kPa), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol.
options.B: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 kPa), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol.
options.C: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature, 0°C and pressure, 1 atm.), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol.
options.D: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 atm.), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol.

questions.explanation: The molar volume of any ideal gas at STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure: 0°C = 273.15 K and 1 atm = 101.325 kPa) is 22.4 L/mol. Option C correctly states both the temperature (0°C) and pressure (1 atm). Option A uses kPa incorrectly (STP is 101.325 kPa). Options B and D use 25°C (which is not STP; that's SATP).

questions.question: Which of the following assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the high compressibility of gases?

options.A: Particles are always in random motion.
options.B: Different particles have different speeds.
options.C: The actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.
options.D: There is no force of attraction between gas molecules.

questions.explanation: The high compressibility of gases is explained by the assumption that the actual volume of gas molecules is negligible compared to the total volume of the gas. This means there is significant empty space between molecules, allowing them to be compressed. Option D explains low density and free movement but is not the primary reason for compressibility.

questions.question: Consider a bottle containing water, water vapor and air in equilibrium. If the temperature decreases slightly, the amount of water vapors;

options.A: will decrease and the vapor pressure will increase.
options.B: and vapor pressure will decrease.
options.C: and vapor pressure will increase.
options.D: will increase and the vapor pressure will decrease.

questions.explanation: When temperature decreases, the equilibrium vapor pressure of water decreases (lower kinetic energy of molecules). Consequently, some water vapor condenses into liquid water, so the amount of water vapor decreases. Both the amount of vapor and the vapor pressure decrease. Options A, C, and D incorrectly describe the direction of change.

questions.question: Why do water droplets collect on the outside of a glass of water on a hot day?

options.A: There will be a condensation of water vapor on the glass.
options.B: There will be a sublimation of water vapor on the outside of a glass.
options.C: There is heat exchange between the water in the glass and the surrounding.
options.D: Water from the glass starts to vaporize.

questions.explanation: On a hot day, the cold glass cools the air surrounding it. When warm, humid air comes into contact with the cold glass, the air temperature drops below its dew point. Water vapor in the air condenses into liquid water droplets on the outside of the glass. This is condensation, not sublimation (which is solid to gas).

questions.question: What are hydrocarbons? Compounds that contain

options.A: benzene rings only.
options.B: benzene and its derivatives only.
options.C: hydrogen and carbon with no benzene rings.
options.D: hydrogen and carbon only.

questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are organic compounds that contain only hydrogen and carbon atoms. This definition includes all types of hydrocarbons: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compounds (which contain benzene rings). Options A and B are too restrictive (only describing aromatic hydrocarbons). Option C incorrectly excludes benzene ring-containing hydrocarbons.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT regarding the boiling points of alkanes?

options.A: Boiling points of straight chain alkanes is greater than that of branched chain alkanes.
options.B: The boiling point of cycloalkanes is higher than that of linear alkanes.
options.C: Boiling points increases with stronger Van der Waals forces.
options.D: Surface area is the only factor that determines the boiling points of alkanes.

questions.explanation: Option D is INCORRECT because surface area is not the only factor determining boiling points. Molecular weight (size), branching, and van der Waals forces also play important roles. While surface area (molecular shape) does affect boiling points, other factors like chain length and molecular mass are also significant. The other statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about minerals and ores?

options.A: Minerals are the natural forms in which various metals exist.
options.B: Ores are usually used to extract metals economically.
options.C: All minerals are ores.
options.D: All ores are minerals.

questions.explanation: Option C is NOT correct because not all minerals are ores. A mineral is a naturally occurring solid with a specific chemical composition. An ore is a mineral or rock that contains a valuable metal in sufficient concentration to make extraction economically viable. Therefore, all ores are minerals, but not all minerals are ores (some minerals are not economically valuable).

questions.question: Why is CaCl₂ added to NaCl in a 1:1/2 ratio in the Down's cell for the manufacturing of sodium metal?

options.A: CaCl₂ is used to lower the density of the mixture.
options.B: CaCl₂ is used as an electrolyte.
options.C: CaCl₂ is used as a catalyst.
options.D: CaCl₂ is used to lower the melting temperature of NaCl.

questions.explanation: In the Down's cell for sodium extraction, CaCl₂ is added to NaCl to lower the melting temperature of the mixture. NaCl melts at 801°C, but with CaCl₂ added (in a 1:1/2 ratio), the melting point is reduced to about 600°C, making the process more energy-efficient. CaCl₂ does not act as a catalyst or change density significantly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major step in metallurgical processes?

options.A: Pretreatment
options.B: Extracting the metal and refining
options.C: Mining the ore
options.D: Concentrating the ore

questions.explanation: Pretreatment is not a standard major step in metallurgical processes. The major steps are: 1) Mining the ore (extraction from the earth), 2) Concentrating the ore (removing impurities), 3) Extracting the metal (reduction to elemental form), and 4) Refining the metal (purification). Pretreatment might occur in some specific processes but is not a general major step.

questions.question: Which monomers are used for the synthesis of Teflon?

options.A: Styrene and Phenol
options.B: Tetrafluoroethylene
options.C: Isoprene
options.D: Propylene

questions.explanation: Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene, PTFE) is synthesized from the monomer tetrafluoroethylene (TFE). The polymerization reaction is: n CF₂=CF₂ → [CF₂-CF₂]ₙ. Styrene and phenol are used for phenolic resins, isoprene for natural rubber, and propylene for polypropylene. Teflon is known for its non-stick properties and chemical resistance.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of an ester having the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₂?

options.A: Ethyl butyrate
options.B: Pentyl butyrate
options.C: Ethyl butanoate
options.D: Methyl butyrate

questions.explanation: The molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₂ corresponds to an ester with 6 carbons. Ethyl butanoate has the structure CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₂CH₃, which has 6 carbons total (4 from butanoic acid + 2 from ethanol). The IUPAC name uses the suffix '-anoate' with the alkyl group first: ethyl butanoate. Option A (ethyl butyrate) uses common (non-IUPAC) nomenclature.

questions.question: What is the formula of pentanoic acid?

options.A: CH₃(CH₂)₂COOH
options.B: CH₃(CH₂)₅COOH
options.C: CH₃(CH₂)₄COOH
options.D: CH₃(CH₂)₃COOH

questions.explanation: Pentanoic acid is a straight-chain carboxylic acid with five carbon atoms. The formula is CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂COOH, which can be written as CH₃(CH₂)₃COOH. Option A (CH₃(CH₂)₂COOH) has 4 carbons (butanoic acid). Option B has 7 carbons (heptanoic acid). Option C has 6 carbons (hexanoic acid).

questions.question: What is the rate of dissolution? It is

options.A: the rate at which a solid dissociates.
options.B: the speed at which a solid sublimes.
options.C: the rate at which a solid turns to liquid.
options.D: the speed at which a solid substrate goes into solution.

questions.explanation: The rate of dissolution is the speed at which a solute (solid) dissolves into a solution. It describes how quickly particles of a solid enter the liquid phase and become solvated. Option A describes dissociation (breaking into ions). Option B describes sublimation (solid to gas). Option C describes melting (solid to liquid).

questions.question: Which one of the following is correctly stated regarding solubility as an equilibrium process?

options.A: Supersaturated solution is a solution that contains more than the equilibrium amount of dissolved solute.
options.B: Supersaturated solution is more stable than saturated solution.
options.C: Unsaturated solution is a solution that is in equilibrium with respect to a given dissolved substance.
options.D: Saturated solution is a solution in which more of the solute can be dissolved.

questions.explanation: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than can be maintained at equilibrium. It is in a metastable state. Option B is incorrect: supersaturated solutions are less stable than saturated solutions. Option C is incorrect: unsaturated solutions are not in equilibrium. Option D is incorrect: saturated solutions contain the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at that temperature.

questions.question: The heating curve shown below shows a substance in the solid, liquid and gas phase. Which segment represents only the liquid phase?
questions.explanation: On a heating curve, segment 3 represents the region where the substance is entirely in the liquid phase and is being heated. Segment 1 is the solid phase, segment 2 is the melting plateau (solid + liquid), segment 4 is the boiling plateau (liquid + gas), and segment 5 is the gas phase. Therefore, segment 3 represents only the liquid phase.
